slides.dek: The gatekeeping made sense in 2005. It does not make sense now.

slides.label: The history
body: Two decades ago a dub meant four voice actors and a script rewritten for weekday cartoon slots. That era trained a generation to say subs or nothing, and the reflex outlived the reason.

slides.label: The present
slides.h: Modern dubs are a different industry.
body: Deep casts, real direction, and simuldubs that land weeks after the Japanese broadcast. Plenty of performances now define their characters as strongly as the original track does.

slides.label: The real rule
slides.h: The best version is the one you [[finish]].
body: Commuting, drawing, folding laundry: a dub turns dead time into watch time. A show finished in English beats a show abandoned in Japanese, every single time.

slides.body: Make your case in the comments. Send this to the friend who says real fans read.
